classification.difficultyReason: Read a piecewise distance–time graph, calculate segment speeds and interpret distance remaining and clock time.

content.prompt: A salesman travelled from town A to town B, which is a distance of 200 km. The graph shows his distance ($d$ kilometres) from town A, $t$ hours after noon.

spec.description: Arrowed axes, labelled time ticks 1–4, distance ticks every 50 km with 100 and 200 labelled, two stationary intervals and four red dashed reading guides. The unlabelled end of the second stationary interval is positioned approximately as drawn; 3.6 is a drawing coordinate, not an additional given.
spec.mathematics: Journey passes through (0,0), (1,50), (2,50), (3,150) and (4,200). It remains at 150 km for an unlabelled interval after t=3 before rising to 200 km.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graph features remain visible in the question edition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: From the graph, find the distance travelled:

answer.worked:
The third hour is from $t=2$ to $t=3$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance travelled}&=150-50\\\text{Distance travelled}&=100\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the speed at which the salesman travelled during:

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find how far from town A the salesman was after 2 hours of travelling.

answer.worked: At $t=2$, the graph gives $d=50$. The salesman was 50 km from town A.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find at what time the salesman was first 50 km from town B.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance from town A}&=200-50\\\text{Distance from town A}&=150\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
The graph first reaches $d=150$ at $t=3$, which is 3 hours after noon: 3:00 p.m.
